title: Use command-line names in missing-argument errors
body:
When a required `param_1` argument is exposed as `param-1` on the command line, omitting it reports the Python attribute name instead of the CLI name. Use the argument's first public name in that error. Regression coverage includes dashed names, an unrelated internal attribute name, and an untransformed-name control. Fixes #1017.

Validation: two new cases fail before the fix, with the control passing. On WSL Linux/Python 3.14.4, 216 related parser/task tests pass and 2 are skipped. Real CLI checks on Windows/Python 3.12.3 and Linux/Python 3.14.4 confirm both the missing-argument error and successful `--param-1`/`--param-2` calls. Black 22.8, the pinned Flake8 4 checks, and mypy 0.971 over all 48 package source files pass. Flake8 used an external entry-point API adapter for this Python 3.12 host, excluding unrelated host plugins. The full unit suite, integrations and older-runtime CI matrix were not run. Based on the 2.2 release line per the contribution guide.
